previousCoordinate.reasonReplaced: The legacy point lay approximately 4.7 kilometres southeast of Værne Kloster and had no source-object contract.

identity.resolvedIdentity: The named Værne Kloster farmyard and manor core at Klosterveien 91, on the former royal estate and site of Norway's only Knights Hospitaller monastery and hospital.
identity.identityProblem: The record combines the medieval monastery, later manor, active private farm, historical estate and a 5,473-decare protected landscape. The coordinate must identify a stable physical core without treating the gameplay radius as the full monastery, estate, property or protection geometry.
identity.splitReason: The monastery traces and later manor developed at the same named core. The wider estate and protected landscape remain larger contextual extents.

evidence.finding: The named farmyard polygon has representative point 59.39354, 10.67424 and is linked to Wikidata Q4994287.
evidence.reason: It directly identifies the current physical manor and farm core.

evidence.finding: The entity links OSM way 124839227 and Kulturminne ID 9570. Its coordinate lies approximately 109.4 metres west of the applied farmyard representative point.
evidence.reason: Confirms the identity and heritage registration of the mapped core.

evidence.finding: SNL identifies Værne as a former royal estate, Norway's only Knights Hospitaller monastery with hospital, later a large manor and farm, and places the foundation in the 1190s under King Sverre.
evidence.reason: Defines the historical identity and warns against reducing the place to the current farm use.

evidence.finding: The source gives Klosterveien 91, gnr. 189/bnr. 1 and notes that the monastery was probably founded late in the twelfth century but may have been established later.
evidence.reason: Confirms the current property identity and supports explicit dating uncertainty.

evidence.finding: The active farm business is registered at Værne Kloster, Klosterveien 91, 1570 Dilling.
evidence.reason: Confirms the current farm and address identity.

evidence.finding: The protected landscape covers approximately 5,473 decares and preserves a manor-shaped agricultural and cultural landscape.
evidence.reason: Establishes that the legal landscape extent is far larger than the gameplay radius and must not be inferred from the point.

evidence.finding: The legacy coordinate lies approximately 4,697.8 metres southeast of the named manor and farmyard core.
evidence.reason: Rejected because it does not identify Værne Kloster.

addressCandidates.rejectionReason: Confirms identity and access context, while the named OSM area supplies the direct coordinate.

sourceObjectCandidates.rejectionReason: Named farm locality point inside the wider site; the farmyard polygon gives the stronger physical core.
Heritage identity cross-check; the linked OSM area provides direct geometry.
Public transport access point approximately 250 metres southwest, not the historical site.
The 5,473-decare protected landscape is a legal and ecological extent, not a point coordinate substitute.
One surviving fragment would reduce the combined monastery, hospital, manor and estate record to one archaeological component.

rawEvidence.description: Persisted manor-core geometry, heritage identity, address, dating uncertainty, wider protected-landscape scope, rejected candidates and access limits.

decision.nextAction: Applied the Værne Kloster farmyard and manor-core point, retained 1190 as an approximate 1190s period anchor and retained the 300-metre gameplay radius. Continue with onsoy_kirke.

notes: The coordinate moves approximately 4,697.8 metres northwest.
The marker represents the named farmyard and manor core, not the complete monastery, estate or protected landscape.
The year 1190 is an approximate period anchor, not an exact foundation date.
The site is an active private farm; the coordinate does not grant access to the yard or buildings.
The radius is not a building, ruin, property, protection, agricultural or monastery-landscape boundary.
